text: "Arrived position 4 mi west of Algiers, Algeria 1705" after 270 miles from Châteaudun-du-Rhumel; from May, "Usual camp duties 4 mi West of Algiers".
source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), Apr-May 1943

text: Beaufighter night fighters at Maison Blanche, the Algiers airfield, with AI radar, working under ground-control stations by call-sign ("Mumsie", "Madbrain", "Funless", "Perform").
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 1

text: F/Sgt G.L. Linklater and Sgt L.V. Anthony up on patrol, 1935-2140.
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 541 (detail of work), AIR 27/1027/38, p. 2

text: "On patrol in Algiers Bay, were told that a number of bandits were 40 miles to the North at 16000ft ... informed that the bandits were 5 miles away at angels 12."
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 2

text: "Thirty bombers raided Algiers during the night of 12 May, scoring hits on the harbor." No units or losses given.
source: German Naval Staff war diary, 12 May 1943 (ONI translation), vol. 45, p. 152

text: "Fired on hostile targets 2050 to 2125 Weather good"
source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), May 1943

text: "The enemy aircraft which was taking evasive action from A.A. turned South about two miles West of Algiers. Our aircraft closed in and gave a two second burst. This was enough and the bandit blew up and fell into the sea. 1 Ju88 destroyed."
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 3

text: "Alerte à Alger": "L'alerte a été donnée dans la soirée à Alger. Des avions ennemis ont survolé la ville. La réaction de la D.C.A. a été très violente et efficace. Quelques bombes ont été lancées."
source: L'Écho d'Alger, 13 May 1943

text: Communiqué no. 188: "La nuit dernière, des bombardiers ennemis ont essayé d'attaquer Alger. Ils ont été chassés par la D.C.A. et les chasseurs de nuit. Trois appareils au moins ont été détruits. Les quelques bombes qui ont été lâchées ont causé un petit nombre de victimes parmi la population civile et de légers dégâts."
source: L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May 1943 (communiqué of 13 May)

text: "Fired on hostile targets 0820 to 0822": two minutes, in daylight; nothing in the paper.
source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), May 1943

text: F/Lt S.S. Duff and Sgt R. Perfect, patrol 1930-2230: "1 JU.88 probably destroyed".
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 541 (detail of work), AIR 27/1027/38, p. 3

text: "Algiers was attacked by 70 Ju 88s. Hits on six steamers were observed." The 13 May entry; most likely this night (13/14 May), possibly a fuller count of the 12th (inferred).
source: German Naval Staff war diary, 13 May 1943, vol. 45, p. 163

text: "Fired on hostile targets 2136 to 2228 Weather good"
source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), May 1943

text: "After a long chase in which no heights were given eventually obtained a visual on a Ju88. He then gave it 3 bursts and although the e/a was badly 'mauled' and lost height, he did not see it fall into the sea and was only awarded a 'probable'."
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 3

text: "Nouvelle alerte à Alger": "Une alerte a été donnée, hier dans la soirée. Un violent tir de barrage de la D.C.A. a accueilli les appareils qui tentaient de survoler la ville. On ne signale ni dégâts ni victimes."
source: L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May 1943

text: Neither the Italian bulletins (nos. 1083, 1084) nor the German communiqués printed on 14 and 15 May mention Algiers: those days they announce the end in Tunisia and raids on Bône, Bougie and Sfax.
source: La Stampa, 14 and 15 May 1943, p. 1

text: W/O R.J. Smith and Sgt J.J. Sanderson scrambled from Maison Blanche, 2205-2325.
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 541 (detail of work), AIR 27/1027/40, p. 1

text: "In the evening of 4 June 19 bombers attacked Algiers. The target was covered by a smoke screen. Two planes are missing."
source: German Naval Staff war diary, 4 June 1943, vol. 46, p. 38

text: "Fired on enemy targets 2225 to 2235 Weather good Morale excellent"
source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), June 1943

text: "At long last the Hun has made an appearance. W/O Smith and Sgt. Sanderson getting their first, a Ju.88 15 miles North of Algiers."
source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/39, p. 1

text: Bulletin no. 1106: "L'aviazione dell'Asse ha bombardato questa notte il porto di Algeri." The German communiqué of 5 June: "Le installazioni portuali di Algeri sono state bombardate la scorsa notte."
source: La Stampa, 6 June 1943, p. 1

text: "Alerte à Alger": "L'alerte a été donnée dans la soirée à Alger. On signale des dégâts et quelques victimes." Admiral Muselier and the inspector general of civil defence went to the damaged areas.
source: L'Écho d'Alger, 5 June 1943

text: "Dans la nuit du vendredi à samedi, quelques appareils ennemis ont lâché des bombes dans la région d'Alger. Il y a eu quelques victimes et des dégâts ont été causés à la propriété civile. Deux bombardiers ennemis ont été détruits."
source: L'Écho d'Alger, 6 June 1943

text: "Après l'alerte de vendredi soir": Generals Giraud and Catroux visited the bombed quarters on the Saturday morning, where clearing and rescue went on; Catroux called on Muslim families who had lost their homes.
source: L'Écho d'Alger, 6 June 1943
